causes.what: The primary database's data volume (fs.data.pct) filled to 100% after climbing steadily for more than an hour, so writes fail. This causes the app 'Database errors', the web-tier and lb-01 5xx, the backed-up job queues and the db-02 replication lag.

evidence: db-01 fs.data.pct was 86.1% at 13:59, 92.8% at 14:29, 99.45% at 14:59 and 100% by about 15:04. That is a steady rise of roughly 0.2% per minute; 'Database volume is almost full' fired at 14:39.
The first symptoms followed the volume reaching 100%: app-01 to app-04 'Database errors' and the lb-01 and web-01 to web-04 5xx alerts at 15:03, then job queue alerts at 15:05 to 15:06.
db-02 replication lag is 356.8s against 2.9s on db-01. The replica is stalling, a consequence of the full primary rather than its own fault. db-02 data volume is only 62%.
db-01 db.conn.count jumped from about 57 at 14:59 to 141.7 now. Connections pile up as the apps retry failed writes.
db-01 CPU (32.7%), I/O wait (7%), slow-query rate (about 2.5) and the nas-01 storage backend (latency 2.9ms, ICMP fine) are all normal. Storage latency and network are ruled out.
I did not check what is writing the data (bloat, binlogs or WAL, backup or a runaway table). The cause of the growth is unconfirmed.
